data.title: Egypt reopens embassy in Libya's Tripoli after 12-year closure
data.description:
Egypt reopened its embassy in Libya's capital Tripoli on Saturday after a 12-year absence, marking a rapprochement with the country's western-based administration, the foreign affairs ministry in Cairo said in a statement.

  • The move marks a shift for Cairo, which has been one of the most prominent backers of eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar, a rival of the Tripoli-based government

  • Egypt closed its Tripoli embassy in 2014, when many foreign missions there closed amid an escalating conflict that saw rival governments set themselves up in the capital and in the east of the huge North African country

  • Egypt's foreign affairs minister Badr Abdelatty was quoted in the statement as saying at the reopening ceremony that the historical significance of the embassy building "aligns with the deep-rooted human and cultural ties that characterize Egyptian-Libyan relations"

  • Oil producer Libya has been plunged into chaos since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011

  • In Benghazi in eastern Libya there is the Libyan National Army under military commander Khalifa Haftar and the House of Representatives, and a government led by Osama Hammad. In the west there is the internationally recognised Government of National Unity headed by PM Abdulhamid Dbeibah and the High Council of State in Tripoli

New York, New York, November 7th, 2026, Chainwire

The first project from Umia's Cohort 1 cleared its minimum raise during the early bid, with more than 200 bidders across three access lanes. The public round on Robinhood Chain is open to everyone until 10 November.

Umia, the onchain platform for launching, funding and governing projects, today opened the public round of the auction for Slop Cash at around 15:35 UTC, after early-bid commitments passed the project's $400,000 minimum raise within 12 hours. Slop Cash is built by Shaw Walters, creator of the open-source AI agent framework elizaOS, and Drew Pierson. It is the first Cohort 1 project to reach auction on Umia, following $UMIA, the first token launched through the system in August.

Slop Cash is a non-custodial funding rail for open-source software. Funding projects put up monthly prize pools against their repositories, and contributors, human or AI agent, work on GitHub as usual. Only merged pull requests and accepted code reviews are scored, in public, and funders sign payouts from wallets Slop Cash does not control.

On Umia, the minimum raise is a structural condition which determines if the launch is successful: had commitments fallen short, every bid would have been refunded in full. With it cleared, the token is now set to launch, deploying the onchain liquidity and placing the project’s domains and social accounts in one legal wrapper under the Umia system. Spending beyond a fixed monthly allowance requires a decision market, where the option the markets value highest is executed.

The early bid ran through three lanes, each with its own cap, and no private round came before it. The Slop community path was reserved for contributors, reviewers and maintainers with accepted work on Slop-listed repositories, who proved their GitHub activity through the Umia Extension. The extension generates a zkTLS proof in the participant's browser, confirming eligibility without the account, login or underlying data becoming visible. That lane filled its $200,000 allocation within the first day. The other lanes served UMIA holders through Umia Pass, and whitelisted funds and angels.

has a total supply of 100 million, of which 45% is offered in the auction and 2% goes to Umia's treasury as launch provider. The token directs Slop Cash's own treasury through decision markets and has no say over contributor payouts, scores or whether a pull request is merged.

"Slop Cash is the first outside project to go through the whole Umia system, from the legal wrapper to the auction to the treasury its token will govern. The early bid put the people who ship the work first in line, and the public round now opens the auction to everyone," said Francesco Mosterts, Co-Founder of Umia.

data.title: Samsung Wallet’s USDC on Solana Is Live — Here’s What the Rollout Actually Covers
data.description:
TL;DR: A Solana Foundation update dated November 5 confirms that Samsung Wallet’s stablecoin account went live on November 2 for eligible US Galaxy owners. USDC transfers and certain international bank payouts are supported, but the headline 82 million compatible devices should not be mistaken for 82 million active users.

A crypto feature that does not feel like a crypto feature may be one of the most consequential ways digital payments reach a wider audience. In a November 5 launch confirmation, the Solana Foundation said Samsung Wallet’s Stablecoin Account became available on November 2. For eligible US Galaxy users, it places USDC inside a familiar wallet app rather than asking them to install and learn a separate cryptocurrency application.

That is a tangible step beyond the launch window described in NewsBTC’s earlier look at Samsung’s planned rollout. But the most useful questions concern what people can do today, who qualifies and what still depends on outside providers.

Transfers without a separate crypto app

The Foundation says eligible users can buy, hold, send and receive USDC over Solana within Samsung Wallet. Bastion provides licensed custody and infrastructure, with Coinbase serving as sub-custodian through Coinbase Prime Vault. That structure matters. Customers see the convenience of a familiar interface, while their assets still depend on a chain of infrastructure and custody providers.

US customers can transfer USDC to other eligible Samsung Wallet users and compatible external wallets. The announcement says Samsung charges no transfer fee for these routes, although other providers may charge fees. A separate path allows eligible users to send funds to qualifying bank accounts in more than 60 countries, potentially arriving as local currency. Available corridors and charges vary by destination; the distinction between a blockchain transfer and a bank payout is important.

The feature sits inside Samsung Wallet’s Quick access area alongside payment cards and everyday credentials. That small interface decision could matter more to adoption than a headline transaction-speed benchmark, because habitual use often depends on how much friction an app removes.

Device reach is not transaction volume

The announcement refers to approximately 82 million compatible Galaxy devices in the United States. That is a ceiling for potential access, not evidence of adoption. It says nothing about the number of activated accounts, transfers completed, average transaction size or users who return the following month.

The eligibility restrictions are also substantial. According to the Foundation, users need to be at least 18, reside in the US, have a Samsung account and use a compatible Galaxy device running Android 13 or later. New York residents are excluded at launch. These requirements make the real reachable population smaller than the device figure.

The payments story extends the institutional work covered in NewsBTC’s report on Solana’s delivery-versus-payment tool, but the two solve different problems. One targets consumer remittances; the other aims at financial-asset settlement.

What success will look like

Samsung has described potential future expansion into online and in-store stablecoin payments and additional markets, subject to regulation. Those ideas are not live features simply because the stablecoin account has launched. Nor should this launch be read as a forecast for SOL’s price: consumer payments can be valuable without creating a predictable relationship between wallet activity and demand for the network token.

A fair assessment will require active-account numbers, real-world fees, payout times, failed-payment handling and whether the feature reduces friction relative to existing remittance services. The verified news is that the service is now operational for a defined group of customers. The commercial test begins after that announcement, when people decide whether to use it again.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Real estate stocks gain as the Blue Wave sends Treasury yields lower
data.description:
Real estate stocks were gaining as the Democrats sweep of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections sent the longer-term Treasury yields down.

Tuesday's midterm results reflected voter frustration over rising prices, the Iran war, and government corruption. The party is positioning itself for an aggressive oversight agenda targeting the Trump administration and powerful special interests.

United States 10-Year Bond Yield hit its lowest level in about two months this week as a collapse in crude oil prices and the midterm elections drained stagflation fears and deficit anxiety, according to a recent report by Investing.com.

Housing-related stocks surged as the elections reignited hopes of several issues plaguing the housing market getting addressed, according to CNBC News.

"Democratic control of Congress raises the potential for lower tariffs, which we estimate represent ~$7,500 of additional cost per home, a de-escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, and a less restrictive approach to immigration policy," UBS reportedly said.

The potential legislations to keep an eye on include the More Homes on the Market Act: a bipartisan bill that would double capital gains exclusions, and the First Home Affordability Act: a 10% first-time homebuyer tax credit, the report noted.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 1.88% week-over-week to 280.25 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF was up 1.92% to $44.00.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index and the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.88% during the course of the week.

Meanwhile, Wall Street's major indexes went from cheerful optimism after the 2026 midterm elections to experiencing their worst day in over a year and a half. The indexes saw severe weekly losses from an ongoing technology selloff and policy fears related to AI.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, American Healthcare REIT led the winners, adding 8.20% to close the week at $57.91. The health care REIT exceeded analyst estimates in terms of third-quarter earnings and revenue.

Equity LifeStyle Properties followed with a 6.64% weekly gain to $62.95.

Iron Mountain (-8.61% W/W to $106.52) topped the decliners despite Q3 earnings surpassing expectations amid a disappointing Q4 guidance.

Data center REITs were declining as the U.S. data center boom faces a fresh political hurdle. The newly elected governors have promised to halt or pause construction across several states, putting a substantial portion of planned development under scrutiny.

Digital Realty Trust (-3.60% W/W to $174.20) was the next major loser in the category.

Park Hotels & Resorts topped the midcap losers, retreating 5.18% to close the week at $15.74. The REIT posted disappointing financial results this week.

data.title: Revised prices on anti-cancer medicines effective from Monday, estimated annual savings of over ₹3500 crore
data.description:
The revised prices on 137 anti-cancer drugs will kick in on Monday, bringing annual savings of over ₹3,500 crore, said a note from the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA).

Drug companies making these medicines were forced to revise prices after the Centre capped trade margins on these drugs at 30 per cent, under the Supreme Court’s watch.

Giving the latest update, the NPPA said on Saturday, about 76 pharmaceutical companies have revised MRPs for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. A reduction has been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50 per cent reduction, and the highest reduction being 96.45 per cent, the NPPA said.

In fact, it said, about 10-15 drugs (of the 137) were yet to be launched in India, and the Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) will be applicable to them when they are brought into the country. According to a source, of 1330 updated prices, about 203 brand prices remain unchanged.

“Every retailer, dealer, hospital and institution is required to prominently display the revised MRP list of anti-cancer medicines on their websites and in their premises,” the NPPA said.

Some of the medicines seeing a reduction in prices included:

# Bevacizumab 100 MG Injection (for Lung, Colon, Ovary and Cervical Cancer) – with Zydus Lifesciences price reducing from ₹ 25,995 to ₹3,318;

data.title: Star Health Settles Over Rs 780 Cr In Cancer Claims In H1 FY27, Women Account For 60%
data.description:
The insurer settles over 85,900 cancer-related claims, highlighting the growing importance of early detection, treatment access and financial protection for women

Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited settled more than 85,900 cancer-related claims worth over Rs 780 crore during the first half of FY2026-27, with women accounting for nearly 60 per cent of the payouts, the company announced on 5 November, 2026. Settlements for women increased 17 per cent year-on-year, while nearly 30 per cent of the total claims were associated with people aged between 51 and 60 years.

According to the insurer, more than 45 per cent of the cancer claim payouts originated from Maharashtra, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The figures highlight the financial support required by patients and families navigating cancer treatment.

A 2013 study published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Prevention, based on Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) National Cancer Registry Programme data from 2001-2004, projected approximately 9.35 lakh new cancer cases among women in India for 2026. Breast and cervical cancers were identified among the leading contributors. The figure represents a projection rather than an observed 2026 count.

Screening And Financial Protection

Government screening initiatives have also expanded. By February 2026, approximately 8.73 crore women had been screened for cervical cancer under the national programme for prevention and control of non-communicable diseases, with 93,062 diagnoses reported.

Star Health said it conducted community health camps during H1 FY27, including initiatives focused on cancer screening and preventive healthcare, to improve awareness and encourage engagement with healthcare services.

Amitabh Jain, Whole-time Director and Chief Operating Officer, Star Health and Allied Insurance, said early detection must be accompanied by access to treatment and financial protection. He emphasised that financial preparedness should support the treatment journey rather than remain an afterthought following diagnosis.

Prof. Dr S. Rajasundaram, Surgical Oncologist, said cancer treatment often involves multiple stages, including chemotherapy, radiation, surgery and long-term monitoring. Financial constraints can lead families to postpone or discontinue treatment, potentially affecting clinical outcomes.

He highlighted health insurance as an important financial cushion that can help families access prescribed treatments and maintain continuity of care. The company said its focus remains on strengthening financial protection and encouraging preventive healthcare awareness, particularly among women.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs flip negative for 2026 after $1.28 billion outflow week, worst since June
data.description:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs logged $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, their worst week since late June, per The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data. It was the funds' second straight negative week and made the top ten largest weekly outflows since they launched in January 2024 at #7.

The funds saw outflows every day except Wednesday last week, per the data. They lost $398.6 million on Monday, $115.6 million on Tuesday, $430.2 million on Thursday and $411.9 million on Friday, with Wednesday's relatively modest $74.6 million inflow marking the only positive day.

The most recent worse week ended June 26, when the funds shed $1.79 billion in what The Block reported at the time was their second-worst week on record. Bitcoin ETFs lost $202.6 million the week before last, including a $643.3 million Friday outflow that was the largest single-day exit in four months after the record Binance hack.

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $403 million of Friday's loss, or about 88% of the day's gross outflows. Bitwise's BITB and Ark & 21Shares' ARKB each lost about $20 million, and Grayscale's GBTC shed $11.1 million. Fidelity's FBTC took in $42.8 million on Friday, after leading Thursday's outflows with $199.9 million, as The Block reported.

Bitcoin funds turn negative for 2026

The week's outflows erased bitcoin ETFs' gains for the year. The funds entered the week with about $368 million in 2026 net inflows, after turning positive for the year in late September. Monday's outflows pushed that figure below zero, and the funds closed Friday at about $914.1 million in net outflows year to date.

The total value of bitcoin held across the 12 funds dropped 2.3% to $95.9 billion, equal to about 6.3% of the cryptocurrency's market capitalization. IBIT held $60.3 billion in net assets against $65.1 billion in cumulative inflows.

The outflows came amid a crypto and equities selloff after Tuesday's midterm elections. Bitcoin fell 5.6% on Thursday alone, and analysts linked the slide to the Democratic sweep of Congress and doubts over AI spending, The Block reported Friday. Analysts say Texas's blue wave in particular could result in slowed development in the state replete with bitcoin mining facilities and data centers.

Ether funds extend losing run to six weeks

Spot ether ETFs lost $365.3 million last week, per SoSoValue data, their sixth straight week of net outflows. The run has drained about $2.02 billion from the funds since late September. Ether ETFs have twice posted eight-week losing streaks, most recently when they matched that record in early July.

Like the bitcoin funds, ether ETFs had only one positive trading day last week, also on Wednesday, when they gained $53 million. Monday's $139.8 million outflow was the week's largest, followed by $100 million on Thursday and $93.2 million on Friday. BlackRock's ETHA accounted for $90.8 million of Friday's total, about 96% of the gross losses, mirroring the firm's bitcoin fund.

The products are now down about $405.6 million for 2026. Net assets fell 2.9% over the week to $12.84 billion, against $11.92 billion in cumulative net inflows.

Solana, Hyperliquid funds post longest outflow runs

Spot Solana ETFs lost $26.3 million last week, per SoSoValue, nearly all of it on Friday. It was their fifth straight negative week, the longest streak since the funds launched in October 2025, and brought five-week outflows to $165.4 million. The streak began the week the funds ended a record 14-week inflow run.

Bitwise's BSOL led Friday's Solana outflows with $14.4 million, followed by Grayscale's GSOL at $5.4 million. The funds held $1.31 billion in net assets as of Friday, down from $1.40 billion a week earlier, though they remain about $676.2 million positive for the year.

The three publicly traded Hyperliquid ETFs shed $15.6 million, also extending their outflow streak to five weeks, the longest since they began trading in May. The funds have lost $58.4 million over that stretch, and their net assets fell about 17% on the week to $374.1 million. Friday's $8 million outflow was led by Bitwise's BHYP.

Bitcoin traded near $75,880 on Saturday morning, while ether changed hands around $2,244, SOL near $89.84 and HYPE around $77.79, according to The Block's price pages.

data.title: Novartis is said to be abandoning Ionis heart drug after late-stage trial setback
data.description:
Novartis is largely abandoning the development of a heart disease therapy discovered by Ionis Pharmaceuticals after the RNA-targeting therapy failed in a late-stage trial last September, Bloomberg reported on Saturday.

The Swiss drugmaker said in a statement that it will discontinue the development of the monthly injection known as pelacarsen for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, a study testing it in a heart valve disease called calcific aortic valve stenosis will continue.

The company didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

In September, shares of Novartis and Ionis fell after the pharma giant said that based on topline data, pelacarsen didn’t meet its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 trial called Lp(a)HORIZON for patients with elevated lipoprotein(a), a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

Amgen , which is advancing its RNA-targeting therapy olpasiran, in partnership with Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals and Royalty Pharma using a similar Lp(a)-lowering approach, also traded lower in sympathy.

On Saturday, Novartis presented full data from Lp(a)HORIZON at the American Heart Association’s scientific sessions in Chicago and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

The data analyzed over a median follow-up of roughly five years confirmed that the antisense oligonucleotide reduced serum Lp(a) levels but without a concomitant reduction in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events such as stroke compared with placebo.

data.title: What should investors do about Canara Bank’s stock?
data.description:
The stock of Canara Bank was trading at ₹100.4 per share when we gave a positive note in December 2024. Since then, the stock is up 22.4 per cent as against the Nifty’s 3 per cent gain in the same period. However, after marking a 52-week high of ₹162.9 in late February 2026, it is down about 32.5 per cent. The price-to-book value ratio at the said peak was 1.23x. Today, the ratio works out to 0.87x.

This largely appears to be reflective of the bank’s weaker performance in terms of net interest income (NII) growth in FY25 and FY26 — the core of any bank’s earnings (see table). Asset quality has continued to improve, and the bank was able to consistently maintain RoA (return on assets) of over 1 per cent, by virtue of lower credit cost and good growth in other income—treasury income and recoveries from written-off accounts in FY25 and gains from IPOs of Canara Robeco AMC and Canara HSBC Life Insurance in FY26. However, in H1 FY27, NII is back to growth, with a rise of 16.9 per cent over H1 FY26. With repo rate hikes, the NIM (net interest margin) trajectory is looking up, although the FCNR(B) leverage loans may partly be a drag on yields.

The bank has meaningfully improved on asset quality and going by a few key metrics, it is placed closer to SBI, which trades at 1.4x (see table). The chief differentiating factors are SBI’s scale and higher CASA ratio (38.3 per cent versus Canara’s 29 per cent), which largely explains its higher margin. If the valuation multiple does not expand and the bank continues to execute well, sustaining its current RoE (return on equity), book value should grow roughly at the rate of RoE, and the stock price can be expected to track that growth.

That said, given the outlook for the bank as found below, the risk-reward equation appears to be favourable at current valuation for investors to consider the stock for the long term.

Recent performance

Here’s how the bank has fared since we last wrote on it.

During FY25-H1 FY27, Canara Bank has grown its advances largely in line with the banking system, while its deposits have lagged the system in FY26 and H1 FY27. Its low credit-deposit ratio of around 75 per cent as of Q4 FY25 and 79 per cent as of Q4 FY26 has allowed it to expand without commensurate rise in deposits. Currently the ratio stands at 81 per cent.

Profit growth has been good in FY25 and FY26, but core NII growth has been flat. This is to do with a drop in NIM from 3.05 per cent in FY24 to 2.51 per cent by FY26. Driven by good growth in treasury income and recoveries from written-off accounts in FY25 and one-off gains from IPOs of its AMC and life insurance associates, profit growth has been decent. Operating expenses have been stable with the cost-to-income ratio at around 48 per cent.

In H1 FY27, NIM improved marginally to 2.53 per cent, on the back of the bank mobilising $5.8 billion of FCNR(B) deposits, which helped replace the rather-expensive bulk deposits. According to the bank, FCNR(B) deposits cost only 6.5 per cent while bulk deposits cost 7.5 per cent. These meant NII grew 16.9 per cent in H1 FY27. However, yields hardening resulted in weaker treasury performance, with other income declining 11.4 per cent. Recoveries from written-off accounts are lumpy and they dropped to 7.8 per cent of operating income (NII plus other income) in H1 FY27 from an average of 10.8 per cent in FY25-26.

Asset quality has consistently improved through H1 FY27, leading to savings on credit cost. Taken together, these push and pull factors have allowed the bank to maintain RoA above 1 per cent. RoE, though lower than before, remains stronger than that of many peers.

Outlook

The management had guided for a loan growth of 11-12 per cent for FY27. However, this earlier guidance may very well be surpassed, given strong demand for credit.

Margin wise, NIM may be expected to inch higher with the RBI having embarked on a rate hike cycle. The share of loans linked to repo rate is a higher 53 per cent for Canara Bank. Transmission of rates on these loans take place as early as the immediately next reset period — which can be monthly, quarterly and so on. Per the management, these loans have completed getting repriced in reaction to RBI’s October 25-basis point (bp) hike and its impact on NIM can be seen in Q3 FY27.

The bank is also seeing robust growth in the retail segment. The segment grew 42.8 per cent in FY25, 32.9 per cent in FY26 and 31.6 per cent in H1 FY27, taking its share of total loans from 16 per cent as of FY24 to 24 per cent currently. Agri, SME and corporate advances account for 22 per cent, 13 per cent and 41 per cent of the loan book. Retail advances carry a yield of 8.65 per cent currently, as against the yield on the overall loan book at 8 per cent. Momentum continuing in retail segment could aid margin. However, the lower spread of FCNR(B) leverage loans (loans advanced to non-residents against their FCNR(B) deposits) of only 40-50 bps, may be a drag on NIM expanding.

With respect to other income, the management assesses that the pool of written-off accounts from which recoveries can be expected is contracting. The related impact can be seen in lower contribution to operating income, going forward. However, yields on G-Secs have fallen from elevated levels seen towards October-end. This can arrest treasury losses. All the above factors could help the bank maintain RoE.

ECL impact

From FY28, banks move to the ECL (expected credit loss) regime of providing for losses on loans (and on investments). The regime, by nature, is more proactive than the current one and so, banks may have to provide more. Canara Bank estimates the one-time transition impact could be as large as ₹12,000-15,000 crore on the net worth or 10-12 per cent of current net worth.

This was, in fact, upped from ₹10,000-12,000 crore a few quarters ago, to accommodate the potential losses on investments held to maturity, due to rising yields. Given that yields have cooled, the bank may revise the estimate downward. Further, the bank expects to stagger the one-time impact over two years, as against the RBI-permitted period up to FY31.

Once transitioned, annual recurring credit cost also is expected to be higher, such that, per the management’s assessment, an RoA of 0.8 per cent may be the new normal for the bank. Higher credit cost under ECL is not specific to Canara Bank alone and applies to the whole banking industry. The management looks to pass this on to the borrower, if the industry decides to do so.

data.title: Carraro India Q2 Net Profit Rises 11% To Rs 35.1 Cr, H1 Income Up 16%
data.description:
Domestic business drives growth as agricultural equipment revenue rises 23 per cent in H1 FY27; company reports margin pressure from higher input and operating costs

Carraro India Limited reported an 11 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 35.1 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 31.7 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Total income rose 19 per cent to Rs 705.8 crore from Rs 593.1 crore.

For H1 FY27, total income increased 16 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,264.4 crore, while PAT grew 9 per cent to Rs 66.5 crore, compared with Rs 60.8 crore in the year-ago period.

EBITDA, including other income, increased 10 per cent to Rs 65.2 crore in Q2 FY27. However, the EBITDA margin declined to 9.2 per cent from 10 per cent a year earlier. For the first half, EBITDA grew 8 per cent to Rs 123.2 crore, with margins at 9.7 per cent against 10.4 per cent in H1 FY26.

Domestic Business Leads Growth

Domestic revenue increased 30 per cent to Rs 865.4 crore during H1 FY27, while exports declined 9 per cent to Rs 375.8 crore.

The agricultural equipment segment recorded 23 per cent growth, with revenue reaching Rs 585.9 crore. Construction equipment revenue rose 8 per cent to Rs 524.3 crore, while other segments grew 13 per cent to Rs 130.9 crore.

Demand for four-wheel-drive tractor axles continued to outperform the overall tractor industry, while the domestic backhoe loader market also witnessed encouraging growth.

Higher Input Costs Weigh On Margins

Commenting on the performance, Balaji Gopalan, Managing Director, Carraro India, said domestic demand remained a key growth driver despite global market uncertainties.

He noted that higher raw material, energy, transportation and conversion costs continued to affect margins. The company is working towards recovering these additional costs from customers while focusing on cost optimisation and operational efficiencies.

During H1 FY27, Carraro India incurred capital expenditure of Rs 20.4 crore, including investments in manufacturing capacity and infrastructure.

The company said its revenue performance remained broadly aligned with its FY27 growth outlook, while margin recovery is expected to be gradual.

data.title: Automakers See Strong Festive Demand As Tata Motors Expects Over 12,000 Dhanteras Deliveries
data.description:
Hyundai expects festive deliveries to rise 14 per cent to 16,000 units, while Mahindra reports near-zero SUV inventory at most dealerships

India's passenger vehicle manufacturers reported strong demand during the Dhanteras and Diwali festive period, with Tata Motors expecting more than 12,000 deliveries on Dhanteras alone and Hyundai Motor India projecting a 14 per cent increase in festive deliveries. Mahindra & Mahindra, meanwhile, said strong demand across its SUV portfolio had brought dealership inventory close to zero across most of its range.

The festive period has provided a boost to retail activity across the passenger vehicle segment, with automakers pointing to sustained customer interest, new product launches and strong demand for SUVs.

Tata Motors Expects Over 12,000 Dhanteras Deliveries

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles expects its single-day deliveries on Dhanteras to cross 12,000 units. The company has recorded retail growth of more than 20 per cent since Ganesh Chaturthi compared with the corresponding period last year.

“The festive season has delivered strong and sustained demand across markets, with customers nationwide choosing our vehicles to mark the occasion. Newly launched products have added further momentum, strengthening traction across the portfolio,” said Amit Kamat, Chief Commercial Officer, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.

Kamat said Dhanteras had witnessed a strong customer response, with deliveries expected to exceed 12,000 vehicles. The company expects the momentum to continue, with Diwali muhurat deliveries scheduled until Wednesday.

Hyundai Projects 14 Per Cent Growth In Festive Deliveries

Hyundai Motor India is also anticipating higher festive deliveries this year. The automaker expects to deliver around 16,000 vehicles across Dhanteras and Diwali, nearly 14 per cent more than the corresponding period last year.

“Dhanteras and Diwali are one of the most auspicious days to bring home a new vehicle and we are witnessing strong customer demand this year as well. We expect to deliver around 16,000 units, nearly 14 per cent higher than last year,” said Tarun Garg, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Hyundai Motor India.

Mahindra Reports Low SUV Inventory Amid Strong Demand

While Tata Motors and Hyundai have shared their festive delivery expectations, Mahindra & Mahindra's commentary points to supply constraints amid strong demand for its sport utility vehicles (SUVs).

Rajesh Jejurikar, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Auto and Farm Sector, Mahindra & Mahindra, said the company had been the fastest-growing brand based on VAHAN registration data for comparable festive days beginning with Navratri, over the approximately 25-day period tracked.

The demand has also translated into lower dealership inventory. According to Jejurikar, physical SUV stocks were close to zero across most of Mahindra's portfolio, with inventory below eight to nine days, excluding vehicles in transit.

“We are operating at full capacity, with our October volumes exceeding the capacity levels we had indicated earlier. Our electric SUV portfolio has also witnessed strong demand through October,” he said.

Mahindra continues to maintain its outlook of mid-to-high-teen growth for its SUV business in FY27, supported by demand across its portfolio, including electric SUVs.

Festive Demand Supports Passenger Vehicle Sales

The three manufacturers' comments indicate continued traction in the passenger vehicle market during one of the industry's key sales periods. While festive deliveries provide a near-term boost to retail volumes, Mahindra's low inventory levels and capacity utilisation also point to the challenge of matching production with customer demand.

With Diwali muhurat deliveries continuing, automakers are looking to sustain the momentum beyond Dhanteras.

Samiksha Choudhary

data.title: Gujarat delegation concludes Australia, New Zealand roadshows ahead of Vibrant Gujarat Summit 2027

Gandhinagar, Nov. 7 -- A high-level delegation of the Gujarat government, led by Minister of Energy and Petrochemicals Rushikesh Patel, has concluded its roadshow in Australia and New Zealand ahead of the Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit (VGGS) 2027, holding 11 one-to-one meetings, four ministerial-level meetings and eight sector-focused roundtables with more than 150 industry, business and government participants.

According to a release, held from October 26 to November 2, the eight-day roadshow also included six site and facility visits and three engagements with the Indian and Gujarati diaspora across the two countries. The outreach aimed to strengthen economic partnerships, attract investments and showcase opportunities in Gujarat across critical minerals, energy, renewable energy, technology, logistics, education, sports infrastructure and tourism.

The delegation included senior Gujarat government officials, Chief Commissioner of State Tax Roopwant Singh, IAS, and Commissioner of Geology and Mining Dhaval Patel, IAS. Industry representatives accompanying the minister included Shreyans Goyal, Chairman and Managing Director of Shakti Group Companies; Mehul Vaidya, Senior Vice President (Project Development) at Reliance Industries Ltd.; Milan Thakkar, Director of Alexius Projects Pvt. Ltd.; and Harshil Tamakuwala, Founder and Director of Hindustan Mag Pvt. Ltd.

During its October 26-30 visit to Australia, the delegation travelled to Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane and held nine one-to-one meetings with companies, investors and institutions, including Cavendish Renewable Technology, Cox Architecture, Initiative Sports & Events, Eyeonic, Progia Foods, Aus Energy Store, the Centre for Australia-India Relations, Endua and Populous.

It also held three ministerial-level meetings with Anoulack Chanthivong, NSW Minister for Better Regulation and Fair Trading, Industry and Trade, Innovation, Science and Technology, Building and Corrections; Warren Kirby, Member for Riverstone and Co-Chair of the NSW Parliamentary Friends of India; and Mark Joseph Coure, NSW Shadow Minister.

Six sector-focused roundtables, hosted by AFL, TerraNext World, the Smart Energy Council and INQ Innovation Global, brought together more than 100 participants from government, industry, academia and startups. The discussions covered sports infrastructure and major events, critical mineral supply chains, renewable energy and innovation-led entrepreneurship.

The programme also included executive dialogues at the second Australia-India Business Meet 2026 in Sydney on commercial partnerships, along with engagements with the Queensland government in Brisbane on resources, energy, sports infrastructure and opportunities linked to the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

The delegation visited Monash University, Cricket Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), Marvel Stadium and Gabba Stadium to study practices relevant to Gujarat's development priorities.

The Australian leg covered critical minerals, energy, technology, education, sports events and infrastructure, and tourism. The delegation also held diaspora engagements in Melbourne and Brisbane, inviting the Indian and Gujarati communities to participate in VGGS 2027 as ambassadors of Gujarat.

In New Zealand, the delegation visited Auckland on November 1 and 2 and held one-to-one meetings with Contact Energy and Service Foods. It also held a ministerial-level meeting with Simeon Brown, New Zealand's Minister of Health, Energy and State-Owned Enterprises.

Two sector-focused roundtables were organised, one on energy and petrochemicals by the India New Zealand Business Council (INZBC) and another by the India New Zealand Chamber of Commerce and Industry (INZCCI). Together, they drew more than 50 participants, including representatives from Mainfreight Air & Ocean, Hiringa Energy, Energy Resources Aotearoa, Bank of New Zealand, Elemental Group and Taranaki Chamber of Commerce.

The delegation also visited Contact Energy's first grid-scale Glenbrook Ohurua Battery project. The engagements covered renewable energy, battery storage, logistics, banking and financial services, scientific research and technology. A diaspora interaction in Auckland connected the delegation with the Indian and Gujarati community in New Zealand.

The roadshow is part of Gujarat's global outreach ahead of the 11th edition of the Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit, scheduled to be held from January 10 to 12, 2027, at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar.

Launched in 2003, the summit is the Gujarat government's flagship platform for investment, business networking and knowledge sharing. The theme for VGGS 2027 is 'Viksit Gujarat-Shaping Global Future.'

data.title: Is AI Taking White-Collar Jobs? What the Latest Numbers Tell Us — WSJ
data.description:
By Ian Hodgson

Consulting firms, law offices and accounting businesses might seem like obvious places for artificial intelligence to shrink payrolls. In October, all three industries added jobs.

Their gains contributed to Friday's brighter-than-expected monthly jobs report from the Labor Department. All told, professional and business services added 70,000 jobs, its largest monthly increase since July 2022.

The gains complicate fears that AI is set to become a white-collar job killer — concerns that helped sweep AI skeptics into office in this week's elections.

Management, scientific and technical consulting services added 17,300 jobs in October over the previous month, while legal services added 2,400 and accounting and related services added 2,300. All are industries frequently ranked as among the most exposed to AI.

"I don't know how you could look at this report and conclude that we're entering anything like a white-collar job apocalypse," said Harvard economist David Deming.

Preston Mui, a senior economist at Employ America, a nonprofit macroeconomic research group, said the report showed little sign so far of the sweeping losses among higher-end white-collar jobs.

"It's not the bloodbath among knowledge workers that a lot of people had feared," Mui said. "At least not yet."

However, those gains run counter to many workers' feelings about the job market — with many companies reluctant to either hire or lay off, many people are having a hard time breaking into the job market or moving up to a better job.

What's more, not all white-collar industries are holding up as well. Newly released September jobs data shows document-preparation services cut employment 17% over the year; telephone call centers and public-relations agencies each lost 4.7%; and advertising agencies shed 3.9%.

Many economists think AI is a particular threat to entry-level, repetitive work — call-center workers, data-entry keyers, junior copywriters — which can be easily automated. At the same time, higher-skill white-collar jobs could benefit from AI if the technology makes them more productive. Lawyers, for example, could spend less time preparing documents and more time advising clients, potentially supporting demand for their services.

"It's changing what employers are looking for," said Cory Stahle, an economist at jobs site Indeed. "They're leaning in to experienced workers and AI skills. What we're seeing are employers adding additional requirements."

While anecdotal reports of AI supplanting jobs abound, economists have struggled to find concrete evidence that it is causing widespread job losses. One complication: Many tech companies overhired coming out of the pandemic, and then began reducing their workforces right around when ChatGPT was first released in November 2022. That means that many layoffs that get attributed to AI could actually just be the result of management miscalculations.

Industry totals can also obscure changes in particular jobs, Mui noted. The figures group workers by their employer's industry, rather than their occupation. A company could, for example, cut administrative positions while hiring for other roles.

"It turns out AI is broad but not that deep. Until it can do the entirety of someone's job, it's hard to plug it in to totally replace a worker," Deming said. "A lot of the jobs we have are about people stuff — forming relationships and building trust. AI can't do that for you."

The AI build-out offers another source of demand for workers: the job of building data centers. Employers added a combined 10,800 jobs in nonresidential builders and specialty trade contractors — workers such as electricians who are in high demand at data-center sites. (Home-building, meanwhile, has been in a slump. Counterparts in residential building shed 16,400 jobs.)

Monthly spending on data-center construction increased by nearly 80% since the start of the year, according to the Commerce Department, while other nonresidential construction slid 4% over the same time.

A July study by Indeed found that job postings mentioning data centers more than doubled between June 2024 and June 2026, while overall postings fell about 12%. Roughly a quarter of data-center postings were for installation and maintenance workers.

The largest data-center building sites employ thousands of construction workers for years, though the facilities employ far fewer people once they are up and operating. Voters on Tuesday backed Democratic candidates who have been critical of data-center construction and pledged to slow it down or pause it.

Write to Ian Hodgson at ian.hodgson@wsj.com

data.title: Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Testnet Step Over Gas-Accounting Risks
data.description:
TL;DR: Ethereum developers have postponed the next Glamsterdam hard-fork step on the Hoodi testnet after researchers identified applications that may depend on gas-accounting assumptions the upgrade would change. The Ethereum Foundation is asking teams to audit code before the process advances.

Ethereum’s next major protocol upgrade has hit an important compatibility check. In a November 6 update, Ethereum Foundation developer Marius van der Wijden said the Glamsterdam testing process would not proceed to the Hoodi fork until problems identified during testing were resolved.

The concern is not that the Ethereum network has stopped functioning. Rather, some existing applications could break because they rely on assumptions about how gas is charged. The Foundation identified EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 as the proposals that require closer scrutiny.

Why a gas change can affect application behaviour

Ethereum gas is commonly understood as the cost of executing transactions and smart-contract operations. Developers also use gas-related properties inside application design and testing. If the protocol alters the accounting model, code built around old assumptions can behave differently even when its business logic has not been edited.

The Foundation said ChainSecurity had found projects that could be vulnerable after Glamsterdam because they depend on invariants that the proposed changes would break. An invariant is a condition developers assume will continue to hold. Breaking one does not automatically mean every affected contract can be exploited, but it can introduce incorrect behaviour, unexpected failures or security exposure.

The engineering team is working with ChainSecurity and Dedaub, alongside internal auditing efforts. It has also published a repository describing eight relevant invariants and examples that developers can check. This is a call for affected application teams to participate in the review, not merely an internal protocol discussion.

A delay can be evidence of a functioning review process

Blockchain upgrades have a difficult obligation: improve the underlying platform without unexpectedly damaging applications already deployed on it. The network is open, and its developers cannot inspect every third-party contract, off-chain integration or custom execution path. Testnets and audits are designed to identify precisely this kind of problem before users face it in production.

The Foundation said AllCoreDevs decided not to fork Hoodi until the issues were resolved, while work on the later Hegota upgrade would continue in parallel. That separation is useful. It suggests the immediate bottleneck sits in the Glamsterdam compatibility review rather than a blanket suspension of all Ethereum development.

For operators, the responsible response is practical rather than dramatic. Teams should check whether their contracts or surrounding code depend on the identified gas assumptions, test against the updated specifications and document any affected flows. Even a contract that appears unchanged could be involved if another component makes assumptions about its gas use.

What the market should watch instead of guessing a launch date

The November 6 post did not establish a new final deployment date, so assigning one would be speculation. The meaningful milestones are revised specifications if necessary, confirmed remediation of affected cases, a successful Hoodi test and clear guidance for applications that may need modifications.

Ethereum’s wider activity continues independently of this testing decision. NewsBTC has recently tracked ETF flows, but fund demand and protocol engineering should not be collapsed into one cause-and-effect story. Here, the verifiable development is a cautious pause after discovering compatibility risk. For a network hosting substantial financial activity, finding that risk before deployment is the critical distinction.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Microsoft Faces AI Backlash as 100+ Protesters Break Into $1B Amsterdam Data Center Project
data.description:
The demonstration brought together environmental campaigners and other protest groups concerned about the industry's growing demand for electricity, water, and land. Police intervened and detained between 150 and 200 people on suspicion of trespassing, according to Dutch authorities.

Protesters Target Microsoft Data Center Construction Site

The demonstration took place at a construction site in Amsterdam's Westpoort district, where Pure Data Centers is developing a facility intended for Microsoft. Members of the Dutch activist group Geef Tegengas entered the site, climbed construction structures and a crane, and displayed banners criticizing artificial intelligence and Microsoft's business activities.

Reuters footage shows around 100 activists breaching a Microsoft data center construction site near Amsterdam on November 6, 2026, protesting the facility's development. Source: Reuters via X

Footage from the scene showed protesters scaling fences, gathering around construction equipment, and displaying messages including "Fuck AI" and "Microsoft Powered Genocide." Some demonstrators also set off flares and spray-painted slogans around the site. The action drew attention to both the environmental impact of data center expansion and concerns about the use of Microsoft's technology in military and surveillance operations.

Sam van der Beek, a protester involved in the demonstration, told Reuters that data centers were "destroying our world" because of the resources they consume. He added that the growing environmental burden was making the planet increasingly difficult to inhabit.

The protest also involved groups opposing Microsoft's connections to military and government surveillance operations. Demonstrators displayed Palestinian flags and banners criticizing the company's services to the Israeli military and the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. These concerns added a human rights dimension to the wider opposition against AI infrastructure.

Police moved to clear the construction site as tensions increased. The Associated Press reported that some activists clashed with officers, while DutchNews reported the use of pepper spray. Dutch police later confirmed that between 150 and 200 people had been detained on suspicion of trespassing. An officer also sustained a minor injury during the demonstration, according to a police statement reported by The Guardian.

Energy and Water Consumption Drive Opposition

Environmental concerns remain at the center of the growing resistance to AI data centers across Europe. Campaigners argue that facilities supporting cloud computing and artificial intelligence require substantial electricity, cooling resources, and land, potentially placing additional pressure on communities already dealing with infrastructure constraints.

Protester Sam van der Beek criticized data centers for their heavy consumption of water, electricity, and land, while the action formed part of a Europe-wide campaign calling for construction to be halted. Source: The Washington Post via X

The Amsterdam project has attracted particular attention because of its expected electricity demand. According to information published by Pure Data Centers, the Westpoort campus will have three towers with a combined data hall capacity of 78 megawatts (MW). The developer plans to connect the facility to the electricity grid through a dedicated substation.

The project's scale has raised questions about how new data centers will compete with households, businesses, and other developments for limited power resources. The Netherlands is already dealing with electricity grid congestion, creating challenges for companies seeking new or upgraded connections. Campaigners argue that allocating substantial capacity to AI infrastructure could make it harder to accommodate other local priorities.

Water consumption is another concern. Data centers require cooling systems to maintain operating temperatures, with demand depending on the technology and cooling methods used. Activists fear that a rapid increase in computing facilities could put additional pressure on local water supplies and environmental resources.

The campaign also challenges the concentration of digital infrastructure within a small number of technology companies. Protesters argue that decisions about where facilities are built and how they operate should involve greater public consultation, particularly when local communities may experience the environmental and infrastructure costs.

$1B Microsoft Data Center Project Raises Regulatory Questions

Pure Data Centers plans to invest more than €1 billion in the Amsterdam Westpoort campus, which is fully leased to Microsoft. The development will consist of three towers, each approximately 85 meters tall, across a site covering around six acres.

The developer estimates that construction and related activities will directly provide more than 1,000 jobs. Once operational, the campus is expected to support approximately 80 permanent positions involving engineering, maintenance, security, and administration.

Electricity requirements remain a central issue in the debate. A Dutch government response to parliamentary questions published in April 2026 stated that the project's grid connection capacity would reach 99 MW, based on 33 MW for each tower. The government calculated that continuous electricity demand at that level would amount to approximately 0.87 terawatt-hours (TWh) annually.

That figure represents a theoretical calculation based on continuous full-capacity consumption rather than verified annual usage. The distinction is important when assessing the project's expected impact on the local power network.

The government also noted that the development would not use groundwater following discussions with the developer. The project was also designed to transfer heat to a planned heating facility across the street, providing a potential use for some of the heat generated during operations.

Amsterdam Data Center Restrictions and Project Approval

The development has also drawn scrutiny because Amsterdam has introduced restrictions on new data center construction. In April 2025, the city barred new data centers and expansions within the municipality until at least 2030, citing concerns over electricity demand and the pressure placed on local resources.

However, the Microsoft-linked project has a longer regulatory history. According to the Dutch government's response to parliamentary questions, the original building permit was requested in December 2019 and granted on November 6, 2020, before the national restrictions on hyperscale data centers took effect.

The national rules, introduced in January 2024, restrict new hyperscale facilities based on specific size and electricity connection thresholds. The government's definition covers projects with more than 10 hectares of built floor space and an electricity connection capacity of at least 70 MW.

Officials said the Amsterdam development does not fall within that legal definition because its built floor area remains below the 10-hectare threshold. The government's explanation indicates that the project's earlier approval and legal classification allowed it to proceed despite subsequent restrictions on large-scale data center development.

The regulatory history has not ended public criticism. Environmental organizations and local campaigners continue to question whether existing approval processes adequately account for electricity demand, land use, and the long-term effects of AI infrastructure on surrounding communities.

Microsoft and Pure Data Centers Respond

Microsoft acknowledged the demonstration and defended the right of people to express their concerns peacefully. However, the company opposed the protesters' entry into the construction site.

"We understand that people feel strongly about the project, and we respect their right to express those views peacefully," a Microsoft spokesperson said. "However, we do not condone any actions that are unlawful or that put people's safety at risk."

Pure Data Centers also called on demonstrators to leave the site safely and offered to discuss their concerns. The company said it remained committed to engaging with local stakeholders and emphasized the importance of maintaining safety at an active construction site.

The developer's position reflects the wider infrastructure industry's argument that data centers provide essential computing capacity for businesses, governments, and consumers. Technology companies consider these facilities necessary to support cloud services, AI applications, and the growing demand for digital processing.

European Opposition to AI Data Center Expansion Grows

The Amsterdam demonstration coincided with the November 6-7 European action days organized by the Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition. The campaign brings together environmental organizations, digital rights groups, and community movements calling for a temporary halt to new large-scale data center construction until stronger environmental and regulatory safeguards are established.

Data centers' water-intensive cooling systems and land-clearing requirements can reduce local freshwater availability and disrupt natural water cycles. Source: Sharon Collins via X

Campaigners organized demonstrations in several countries, including Germany, Poland, Ireland, Italy, and the United Kingdom. Their demands include greater transparency, more public involvement in planning decisions, and clearer requirements for electricity and water consumption.

The campaign has also highlighted concerns about whether the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is compatible with Europe's climate objectives. Data centers are becoming an increasingly important part of the region's digital economy, but their growing energy requirements have prompted questions about grid capacity and the availability of renewable electricity.

European policymakers face the challenge of expanding computing infrastructure while protecting consumers and local communities from additional environmental and energy pressures. EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen has argued that Europe needs more data centers to develop its own AI capacity while warning that expansion must not drive up electricity bills, increase the risk of power shortages, or damage the environment.

The Amsterdam protest illustrates how these competing priorities are becoming increasingly difficult to reconcile. With Microsoft-linked construction continuing despite local opposition, the debate over AI infrastructure is moving beyond technology investment and into questions of environmental responsibility, public oversight, and corporate accountability.

data.title: Utilities Earnings Scoreboard: 86% beat EPS estimates, 93% post Y/Y earnings growth

data.title: Bank of Baroda’s Guyana subsidiary opens new Head Office, Georgetown branch
data.description:
Bank of Baroda (Guyana) Inc, a wholly owned subsidiary (WOS) of Bank of Baroda (BoB), inaugurated its new Head Office and Georgetown branch, along with the BoB Heritage Centre.

BoB’s WOS operates two branches in the South American country. It is the only Indian bank with a presence in Guyana.

Debadatta Chand, Managing Director & CEO, BoB, said, “Our relationship with Guyana is older than its independence. We have grown alongside this country and have been part of its economic and financial journey. As an Indian bank with deep roots in Guyana, Bank of Baroda is proud to be a financial bridge connecting these two friendly nations.”

The bank started operations in Guyana on March 31, 1966, nearly two months before Guyana attained independence. In 1999, the public sector bank’s local operations were converted into a wholly owned subsidiary, Bank of Baroda (Guyana) Inc.

Chand said digital payments is a key area of focus for BoB’s WOS, particularly in view of Guyana’s introduction of real-time payment system. He said, “Following the understanding between India and Guyana, efforts are underway to facilitate UPI-based payment capabilities in Guyana.”

“Bank of Baroda would be keen to contribute to this initiative in coordination with NPCI, the relevant authorities and other stakeholders. The recently announced US$500 million Indian credit facility for key development projects in Guyana represents another important milestone in this partnership... We want to grow with Guyana, serve its people and contribute to its prosperity.”

data.title: Assam: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal meets injured in Tengakhat tank farm fire, reviews medical care
data.description:
Dibrugarh, Nov. 7 -- Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Saturday met those injured in the explosion and fire at Oil India Limited's Tengakhat Tank Farm in Assam's Dibrugarh district and reviewed their medical treatment at Aastha Hospital.

Sonowal interacted with doctors and the hospital administration to take stock of the condition of the injured and the progress of their treatment. He prayed for their speedy and complete recovery.

Speaking about the incident, the Union Minister said seven people were severely injured in the fire and explosion that occurred on Friday. Of them, three have died, while the remaining four are in critical condition.

"In the incident that occurred yesterday in Tengakhat, 7 people were severely injured. So far, 3 individuals have passed away, and the remaining 4 are in critical condition. This is a deeply tragic event," he said.

Sonowal urged Oil India Limited to ensure advanced medical treatment for those in critical condition and provide appropriate compensation to the families of those who lost their lives.

"We urge Oil India Limited to accord due significance to this incident. Appropriate compensation must be provided to the families of those who lost their lives. Those in critical condition must receive high-quality medical care; Oil India should ensure that advanced treatment is arranged for them. An investigation must be conducted to determine the causes behind this incident," he said.

In a post on X, Sonowal said he had spoken over the phone with the Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of Oil India Limited to take stock of the explosion and fire at the Tengakhat Tank Farm.

He said he had urged the CMD to ensure the best possible medical care for the injured and adequate compensation for the families of those who died.

The Minister also called for a high-level inquiry by the concerned department to establish the exact cause of the incident and investigate all related aspects.

Sonowal extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.

data.title: Earnings scorecard: 20 out of 21 technology companies beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
Information technology stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major companies, including Apple , Palantir Technologies , Advanced Micro Devices , and Super Micro Computer .

The information technology sector gained nearly 15.65% so far this year, outperforming the broader S&P 500 Index, which rose about 7.4%.

In this week's earnings recap, 21 tickers reported results, of which 20 companies beat earnings estimates, while Trimble reported EPS in line with market estimates. On a year-over-year basis, 20 out of 21 companies reported earnings growth.

On the revenue front, all 21 tickers beat Wall Street's expectations and also posted year-over-year revenue growth.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players that reported results this week:

Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that topped Wall Street's estimates.

For the period ending Sept. 26, Apple said it earned $2.10 per share as revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $114.48B. Included in that was $57.58B from the iPhone, above Wall Street's estimate of $56.49B.

Apple offered stronger-than-expected guidance on the earnings call, due in part to continued momentum in the iPhone. It expects revenue to grow between 7% and 10% year-over-year, above the 6% estimate. However, gross margins are expected to be between 45% and 46%, below Wall Street's forecast of 46.9%.

Palantir reported stellar third-quarter results and raised its full-year guidance above Wall Street's forecast.

For the period ending Sept. 30, Palantir said it earned an adjusted $0.44 per share as revenue soared 96% year-over-year to $2.31B. Included in that was a 119% rise in U.S. revenue to $1.937B. U.S. commercial revenue grew 148% year-over-year to $984M, while U.S. government revenue grew 96% year-over-year to $953M.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, Palantir expects revenue to be between $2.649B and $2.653B, above the $2.46B estimate. Adjusted operating profit during the period is expected to be between $1.64B and $1.644B, above the $1.41B estimate.

AMD reported third-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's expectations.

For the period ending Sept. 26, AMD said it earned an adjusted $2.09 per share as revenue rose 45% year-over-year to $13.38B. Data Center revenue rose 97% year-over-year to $8.55B, aided by its MI-series AI accelerators and its Instinct and EPYC processors. Analysts were anticipating $8.2B in data center revenue.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, AMD expects revenue to be $17B, plus or minus 3%, above the $16.29B estimate. Adjusted gross margin is expected to be roughly 55%, AMD added.

For the upcoming week, Applied Materials and Cisco Systems are among the key information technology companies scheduled to report quarterly results.
